page_title: VoiceStudio — Real-Time Broadcast Voice Rack for macOS

sources.entry: VoiceStudio - Real-time broadcast voice rack in Swift and CoreAudio with subtle pitch depth, sub-harmonic warmth, 6-band EQ, de-esser, and compressor for Discord, Zoom, Teams, and OBS. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/saadmsft/VoiceStudio) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: VoiceStudio
summary.one_liner: A native macOS real-time voice processing app that runs a broadcast-style effects chain (pitch, EQ, de-esser, compression) on your microphone for use in video calls and streaming apps.
use_cases: Make a thin laptop microphone sound warmer and clearer on calls
Process mic audio for Discord, Zoom, Teams, Slack, Meet or OBS
Route processed voice to a virtual mic such as BlackHole
Tune voice EQ and dynamics live while recording short clips
Apply subtle pitch depth to a spoken voice
summary.what_it_does: The page describes a native Swift and CoreAudio app that processes microphone input in real time. The effects chain includes a pitch shift (about -0.65 semitones, described as the sweet spot), a sub-harmonic octave exciter, warm tube drive, a 6-band parametric EQ with cuts near 80 Hz and 310 Hz and a boost near 4.2 kHz, a split-band de-esser, and a compressor. It can record a 5-second sample, mute the virtual mic output during that time, and loop it for tweaking. Routing uses CoreAudio AUHAL to send audio to BlackHole 2ch while leaving the default speakers and headphones unchanged. The page lists 0.4% idle CPU and installation via Homebrew cask.
notable: Native Swift and CoreAudio engine at 48 kHz with 0.4% idle CPU claim
Routes to BlackHole 2ch via AUHAL without changing default speaker output
Listed in awesome-mac as open-source freeware
caveats: Requires BlackHole 2ch for virtual mic routing, as named on the page
